Since 2015, Mejuri has reimagined what fine jewelry can be in a modern world—shifting it from a traditional gift to to a personal choice rooted in self-expression.
 Founded by third-generation jeweller Noura Sakkijha, the brand was built on a simple idea: fine jewelry shouldn’t require a special occasion, and it should never come with guilt. It’s about celebrating yourself—your style, your life, your everyday.
 Mejuri meets customers where they are—online, in app, and through a growing global retail footprint of 58+ stores worldwide. Mejuri is also deeply committed to doing things the right way, with responsible sourcing, sustainable practices, and philanthropic initiatives that reflect our values and long-term vision.
 Job Overview
 6 Month Contract 
 The Growth Marketing Specialist (6 months) owns the performance of Mejuri's paid social channels (Meta, TikTok and Pinterest) and is accountable for the net merchandise value, incremental return on ad spend, and digital traffic they deliver. The role also owns the paid social testing roadmap, including early tests on emerging platforms like YouTube and Reddit.
 You'll build, launch and optimize campaigns yourself and manage day-to-day spend within the allocations your manager sets. You'll report to the Manager, Growth Marketing, and present results to the VP of Growth. Your closest partner is the Creative team, and you'll also work with Brand, Organic Social, Influencer Marketing, E-commerce and Merchandising, and Data and Analytics, as well as platform reps at Meta, TikTok and Pinterest.
 The Growth Marketing Manager sets channel strategy and cross-channel budget. You run the channels day to day and bring the data-backed recommendations that decide where they go next.
 What you'll do 
 Running Paid Social 
 Campaign execution: Campaigns go live correctly and on time for every drop, launch and commercial moment. You build and traffic them yourself, including manual ad uploads.
 Budget pacing: Spend lands on plan each month. You check pacing daily and adjust bids and budgets within each channel's approved allocation.
 Optimization: Spend moves toward what's working. You pause underperforming ads, rotate creative, and act on in-flight performance without waiting for sign-off.
 Platform issues: Ad rejections, tracking gaps and data discrepancies get resolved without holding up a launch. You work through them directly and escalate only when a cross-team decision is needed.
 Testing and Learning 
 Test roadmap: Each quarter starts with a prioritized list of creative, audience, format, bidding and placement tests. You build and maintain the list and agree on priorities with your manager.
 Test design: Test results hold up. You write the hypothesis, set up a clean test, and wait for statistical significance before calling the result.
 Emerging platforms: Mejuri learns whether channels like YouTube and Reddit are worth scaling. You propose and run the tests that answer that question.
 Recommendations: What you learn turns into decisions. You bring data-backed proposals, such as scaling an audience or adopting a new format.
 Partnering With Creative and the Business 
 Creative feedback: Creative knows what's working and why. You give specific, actionable reads by creative, format and placement, and contribute to briefs.
 Brand and performance: Campaigns reflect Mejuri's identity and still drive revenue. When the two pull in different directions, you find the version that serves both.
 Launch priorities: Traffic goes to the products and launches that matter most. You align with E-commerce and Merchandising on priorities, landing pages and inventory.
 Reporting: Your manager, the Growth team and Finance have an accurate read on performance and pacing. You report weekly and recap each channel monthly.
 What you'll bring to the team 
 Hands-on paid social experience: 2–4 years personally building, launching and optimizing campaigns in Meta Ads Manager. TikTok or Pinterest experience is strongly preferred. Agency experience counts if you did the work yourself.
 Budget accountability: You've managed a monthly budget of [$250k+] and been responsible for its pacing and reallocation.
 Analytical rigor: You build your own reports in advanced Google Sheets or Excel, break performance down by creative, audience and placement, and design and read A/B tests, including basic statistical significance.
 Measurement fluency: You understand attribution windows and the difference between platform-reported results and incremental impact.
 Brand and creative judgment: Brand-side DTC or e-commerce experience, ideally where content and creative drive results, and a record of creative feedback that teams acted on. Experience in jewelry, luxury, fashion or beauty is a bonus.
 Clear communication: You can turn performance data into plain-language insight that creative and brand teams can act on.
 Nice to have: SQL, a BI tool, Shopify, pixel or Conversions API troubleshooting, lift studies, creative analytics tools, and experience using AI tools to speed up analysis

About AI Acquisition 
 AI Acquisition is a bootstrapped, founder-led business helping founders and operators scale with AI, combining a sales and delivery engine, one-to-one consultation, and our own SaaS platforms. We move fast, we build constantly, and we hold a high bar for the people who work directly with our clients.
 We currently manage thousands of active clients across multiple products, with 250+ new clients onboarding every month. The Account Management function is the front line of that relationship.
 The Role 
 You are the person between the client and the outcome. Not a relationship manager. Not a check-in scheduler. Not someone who forwards tickets and hopes for the best.
 You own a portfolio of clients who are building real businesses with our support. Some are launching for the first time. Some are scaling. Some are stuck and frustrated. Your job is to diagnose where they actually are, figure out what's blocking their progress, manage their expectations when needed, and drive them toward commercial results, not just activity.
 This means you need to understand marketing, sales, offer development, and fulfillment well enough to have real conversations about all of them. If a client's campaign is generating calls but nobody's closing, you need to be able to tell them why and what to do about it, not pass it to someone else.
 Our clients purchase a fully built AI lead-generation business: brand, website, funnel, lead engine, and the systems that help turn leads into customers. You own the relationship around that delivery. You need to know what they bought, what was promised, where they are in the journey, and what needs to happen next, with specifics, not generalities.
 You'll work directly with clients on Zoom, Slack, and through our internal systems. You'll run growth workshops, intro calls, and quick syncs. You'll manage escalations without panicking and celebrate wins without coasting. And when a client is about to walk, you'll be the person who finds the path to keep them or makes the honest call that they should go.
 What You'll Own: 
 A portfolio of active clients across different stages: onboarding, growth, scale, and at-risk
 Growth workshops, intro calls, and regular check-ins; you set the rhythm, not the client
 Client expectation management, framing what's realistic, resetting when needed, never overpromising
 Diagnosing why a client isn't getting results: is it the offer, the funnel, the sales process, the client's own execution, or something upstream?
 Funnel and campaign literacy and understanding the client's lead engine (Meta ads, cold email, B2B book-a-call, DFY website), confirming it matches their contract and guarantee, and flagging mismatches before they become problems
 Reading the client's specific contract, understanding the distinct payment flows (client pays AIA, client's customers pay client, ad spend reimbursement), and giving accurate answers under pressure rather than quoting generic numbers
 Spotting the signals before a client escalates (sudden silence, short replies, frustration, refund language, contract/funnel mismatches) and acting on them with a structured escalation, not a panicked message
 De-escalating frustrated clients without throwing the company under the bus, without panicking, and without making promises you can't keep
 When you inherit accounts, you verify every client's status, contract, delivery stage, and risk level before assuming anything is fine
 Spotting when a client is ready for more and positioning it as the natural next step, not a sales pitch
 Every client interaction, decision, and next step logged in our systems (Athena ticketing, Slack channels)
 Collaboration with the broader CS, delivery, and onboarding teams to make sure nothing falls through the cracks
 What We Need From You 
 4+ years in a client-facing account management, CSM, or business consulting role where you were directly responsible for client outcomes, not just client satisfaction scores
 You've consulted business owners on how to start, grow, or scale a business, walked them through the hard parts, not just handed them a playbook
 You understand (or can learn fast) the mechanics of B2B lead generation: Meta ads, cold email campaigns, funnels, and how they connect to a client's revenue. You don't need to run campaigns yourself, but you need to diagnose why one isn't converting and have a real conversation about it with the client
 You're comfortable navigating money conversations with clients, not quoting generic numbers, but reading the specific contract, understanding the payment flows, and giving accurate answers under pressure
 You can manage difficult client conversations with composure, you stay calm, you don't blame, you find the path forward
 You come with solutions, not just problems. When something breaks, your instinct is to propose a fix, not report the issue and wait
 You're confident on camera and on calls; clients trust people who sound like they know what they're doing, even under pressure
 You've worked in a startup, agency, or fast-moving environment where things change fast and you had to figure things out without a manual
 You're comfortable with AI tools and either already use them in your workflow or are the kind of person who finds and tests them without being told to
 You don't need to be chased. You manage your own time, your own portfolio, and your own follow-ups
 This Is Not For You If: 
 You only know one side of the equation (only marketing, or only sales) and aren't interested in learning the other
 You need everything documented before you can act; we're building the playbook, not following one
 You wait for clients to come to you with problems instead of spotting them early
 You avoid hard conversations or default to telling clients what they want to hear
 You treat AI as a buzzword rather than something you actually use
 You need heavy management and regular direction to stay productive
 You hear "refund" and freeze instead of diagnosing what went wrong and whether it's fixable
 What Success Looks Like: 
 Your clients are progressing; not just happy, but actually hitting milestones and getting results
 Escalations that reach you don't reach anyone above you, you resolve them
 You're the AM other people point to when asked "who handles clients well here"
 You identify upsell opportunities because you actually understand where the client is and what they need next
 Clients at risk are flagged before they ask for a refund, not after
 You can audit a new book of business end to end and produce an accurate status picture within your first week of owning it
 Your documentation is clean, current, and useful; anyone picking up your account can see exactly where things stand
 You adopt new tools and processes fast and bring ideas for improving them
 Our Process 
 After an initial screen, you'll complete a scenario-based Loom task, a real client situation that tests how you diagnose problems, manage expectations, and make commercial decisions. If you pass, you'll meet with our CS Leadership team for a deeper conversation.
 We assess for judgment, not just experience. Show us how you think.
 The Environment 
 This is a high-performance, remote-first team operating at the cutting edge of AI-powered business building. Here's what that means for you:
 Direct access to founders from day one, no layers, no politics. You'll work alongside people who are building the business, not managing from a distance.
 Real growth path, strong performers are promoted from month three, not year three. We move people up based on what they deliver, not how long they've been here.
 Exposure to AI-led systems and tools, you won't just use AI as a buzzword on your CV. You'll operate inside a business that builds and ships AI products daily, and you'll be expected to use them to get better at your job.
 Compensation that rewards output, base plus performance bonus plus upsell commission. The harder you push, the more you earn.
 Autonomy and ownership, you manage your portfolio, your time, and your client relationships. No micromanagement, no hand-holding.
 A team that holds a high bar, the people around you are operators, not passengers. That's the standard, and it's what makes this place worth being in.
If you're looking for structure handed to you, this isn't the right place. If you want to be the one " Lifting up the hood ", build something real, and raise the bar every week with a team that moves fast - we want to talk.

 THIS IS AN UNPAID VOLUNTEER ROLE. 
 About DTID
 The Digital Technology Institute for Development (DTID) is an international non-profit institute advancing the responsible use of artificial intelligence, blockchain and emerging digital technologies to support sustainable development and policy implementation.
 DTID brings together professionals, researchers, technology specialists and other stakeholders to generate research, develop practical solutions, strengthen partnerships and support informed decision-making at the intersection of technology, climate change and sustainable development.
 The Role
 DTID is seeking an experienced, innovative and technically accomplished Chief Technology Officer (CTO) to provide strategic and technical leadership across the organisation's emerging technology portfolio.
 Reporting directly to the Director-General , the CTO will lead DTID's work across Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT)/Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), Data Science, Big Data Analysis, Data Modelling, Quantum Computing and technology standards .
 The successful candidate will be responsible for defining DTID's technology strategy, overseeing technology research and development, leading technical teams and translating emerging technologies into practical solutions that support climate action, sustainable development and policy implementation.
 The CTO will also oversee the development of Proof-of-Concepts, pilots and technology applications; strengthen DTID's internal technical capabilities; develop strategic partnerships; and provide technical leadership across multidisciplinary projects.
 Strong practical proficiency in blockchain development and programming is essential for this role. Experience developing artificial intelligence or machine-learning solutions is highly desirable. 
 This is a senior leadership position requiring strong technical expertise, strategic thinking, people leadership and the ability to communicate complex technology concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
 Key Responsibilities
 The Chief Technology Officer will:
 Define and lead DTID's technology strategy and roadmap across blockchain, artificial intelligence, IoT, data technologies, quantum computing and related emerging technologies.
 Lead and manage DTID's emerging technology teams and standards-development activities, including recruitment, onboarding, mentoring and capability development.
 Oversee the design, development, testing and deployment of Proof-of-Concepts, pilots and technology solutions.
 Guide the application of DLT/Blockchain, AI, machine learning, data science, data modelling, IoT and other emerging technologies across DTID projects.
 Ensure appropriate standards for the quality, reliability, security, scalability and documentation of DTID's technology products and solutions.
 Monitor and evaluate the performance and impact of technology initiatives and recommend improvements where appropriate.
 Provide technical leadership and guidance to Technology Officers and multidisciplinary project teams.
 Identify and develop strategic technology partnerships with research institutions, technology organisations, governments, international organisations and other relevant stakeholders.
 Monitor emerging technology trends and assess their potential application to climate action, sustainable development and public policy.
 Represent DTID at relevant conferences, technical forums, stakeholder meetings and external engagements.
 Contribute technical expertise to DTID research, publications, standards, proposals and institutional initiatives.
 Collaborate with the Director-General and other senior leaders to ensure technology priorities support DTID's wider strategic objectives.
 Skills and Abilities
 Candidates should demonstrate:
 Excellent written and spoken English.
 Strong strategic and technical leadership capability.
 Excellent analytical, mathematical and problem-solving skills.
 Strong software-development and technology architecture capability.
 Ability to lead, mentor and develop multidisciplinary technology teams.
 Excellent organisational and time-management skills.
 Ability to manage multiple technology projects and competing priorities.
 Strong project-management and delivery capability.
 Ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear information for non-technical audiences.
 Strong professional communication, presentation and stakeholder-engagement skills.
 Ability to build constructive relationships with senior internal and external stakeholders.
 Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgement and take ownership of strategic priorities.
 Ability to lead effectively within a remote and internationally distributed organisation.
 Strong research capability and ability to evaluate emerging technologies and technical approaches.
 A creative, innovative and solutions-focused approach to technology development.
 Ability to commit an average of approximately 20 hours per week to the role.

 Distributed Ledger Technology and blockchain architecture.
 Blockchain programming and smart-contract development.
 Artificial intelligence and machine learning.
 Internet of Things technologies and architectures.
 Data science, data analysis and data modelling.
 Big-data technologies and data engineering.
 Quantum computing and emerging quantum applications.
 Cloud architecture and cloud-computing platforms.
 Cybersecurity, information security and data governance.
 Technology standards and responsible technology governance.
 Agile technology-development methodologies.
 DevOps, software architecture and technology product development.
 Technical experience should include relevant programming languages, frameworks and platforms such as:
 Solidity and Ethereum or comparable blockchain environments. 
 Python, R or other relevant programming languages. 
 TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn or comparable AI/ML frameworks. 
 APIs and data formats including JSON, XML and CSV .
 Cloud platforms including AWS, Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud Platform .
 GitHub and other version-control or open-source development environments.
 A portfolio of supported open-source projects, GitHub contributions, Proof-of-Concepts or deployed technology solutions would be advantageous.
 Knowledge of climate change, sustainability, climate finance, international development and digital policy would also be highly desirable.
 Education and Training
 Candidates should preferably possess:
 A Master's degree or equivalent postgraduate qualification in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Software Engineering or another relevant technical discipline .
 A PhD, MBA or other advanced qualification relevant to technology leadership, emerging technologies or innovation would be advantageous.
 Relevant professional certifications in areas such as:
 Blockchain technologies.
 Artificial intelligence and machine learning.
 Cloud computing.
 Cybersecurity.
 Data science.
 Technology architecture.
 Agile or project management.
 would also be beneficial.

 Professional proficiency in English.

 Senior-level experience leading technology teams, technical projects or digital innovation initiatives.
 Demonstrable practical experience in blockchain development and programming .
 Experience designing, developing and deploying technology applications, Proof-of-Concepts or digital solutions.

 Experience with project planning, budgeting, reporting and technical documentation.
 Experience working with cloud infrastructure and modern software-development environments.
 Experience developing technology strategies, roadmaps or architecture.
 Experience engaging senior stakeholders, external partners and technical specialists.
 Experience identifying and developing strategic technology partnerships.
 Experience conducting or overseeing technical research and innovation initiatives.

 Contribute directly to DTID's technological capability, institutional development and international impact.

 This is an unpaid volunteer position.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. 
 An overview of this role
 As an AI Transformation Owner at GitLab, you'll shape your function's AI strategy and build the solutions that deliver it. You are the person responsible for identifying where AI can fundamentally change how your org operates, partnering with your Executive Sponsor to align on the biggest challenges, and driving measurable outcomes against them.
 Think of this as a product management role where the product is your org's way of working. You'll manage the full lifecycle: understanding how work flows today, deciding where AI should reshape it, prioritizing what gets built and in what order, and ensuring what ships actually gets adopted. You'll also prototype solutions, configure agents, and prove what's possible before pulling in engineering support to scale it.
 You will work closely with an AI Engineer who sits within the Enterprise AI team. Together you form a partnership: you bring the business context, process intelligence, and strategic prioritization. They bring the technical depth, production-grade delivery, and architecture decisions. You'll build working solutions at the no-code and low-code layer, and partner with the AI Engineer on the right approach, tooling, and structure.
 What you'll do
 Strategy & Prioritization
 Own your function's AI strategy, aligned with your Executive Sponsor and business priorities. Understand which metrics matter to the org, identify what will move the needle, define how you'll measure impact, and track progress over time.
 Map how work flows across your function end-to-end, including the handoffs upstream and downstream to other orgs. Identify where the real constraints are, not just the ones your team can see. Focus on the 100x problems: where could leveraging AI in a workflow let your org execute it orders of magnitude faster, or at 100x more volume than before?
 Manage intake of AI requests, ideas, and pain points from across the function, including via your Champion network. Ensure every team member has a clear route to surface what they need, rather than building independently.
 Prioritize strategically against business outcomes and executive guidance. Hold the line on priorities - we cannot change direction every two weeks - and ensure the AI Engineer's time is spent on the highest-impact work.
 Adoption & Change Management
 Reimagine, not just automate. Challenge your org to think beyond injecting AI into existing workflows. Work with Enterprise AI to spot opportunities to fundamentally rethink how work gets done.
 Drive adoption and change management together with the AI Engineer. The best AI solution is worthless if nobody uses it. Create the channels, rituals, and feedback loops that make AI visible in your function: shared spaces for teams to show what they've built, regular office hours, onboarding for new hires, and celebration of wins. Own the rollout and iteration needed to make AI initiatives stick.
 Coordinate with Enterprise AI to ensure your function benefits from patterns, tools, and learnings emerging across other parts of the business.
 Build and bridge the Champion network in your function. Champions are the peer community that extends your reach beyond what you and the AI Engineer can deliver directly. From early in the role, identify and recruit Champions across sub-teams (5-10% time, formally agreed with their manager), run a regular Champion sync, host demos to the wider function, and act as their bridge to Enterprise AI. Champions are not your reports: you coordinate them, you don't manage them. Without this network, your reach is capped.
 Hands-On Building & Agent Operations
 Build AI agents using no-code and low-code platforms (e.g. Glean, Workato, similar tools). Go from idea to working prototype without waiting for engineering.
 Author and iterate on skills files that define how AI agents behave. Refine instructions based on real usage and share reusable skills across the function.
 Configure MCP servers and tools, giving agents access to the business systems they need. Partner with the AI Engineer on what to connect and how to do it securely.
 Own your function's fleet of agents. Some agents will be used directly by people in your org. Those that aren't, you own. Either way, you're accountable for their performance: tracking KPIs, running evaluations after model or data changes, and iterating based on what you learn.
 Expect to rebuild. AI tools and models evolve fast. The agent you built last month may need to be replaced, not patched. You should be comfortable sunsetting your own work when a better approach emerges, and helping your org stay current rather than attached to what exists today.
 What you'll bring
 Business & Strategic
 Deep knowledge of your function's operations. You understand how work moves through your org, where it gets stuck, and why. You can trace a process end-to-end and explain how it connects to the teams around it.
 Strategic prioritization skills. You've managed competing demands before and can make hard calls about what matters most. You think in terms of business outcomes, not activity.
 A product management mindset. You naturally think about intake, backlog, iteration, and adoption. You're comfortable defining success metrics and holding yourself accountable to them.
 Strong communication and influence. You'll be the person saying "not yet" to some teams and "think bigger" to others. You need the credibility and interpersonal skills to make both of those conversations land.
 Cross-functional instincts. You default to understanding how your org's processes affect and are affected by the teams around you - not just optimising in isolation.
 Experience building peer networks or communities of practice. You've recruited and sustained volunteer contributors before, whether as a guild lead, champion program owner, or community organizer. You know how to motivate people whose time you don't directly own.
 Hands-On & Technical
 Comfortable building with AI tools. You don't need to write production code, but you should be able to build a working agent, configure a skill, connect an MCP server, and troubleshoot when something isn't working. Think: power user, not software engineer.
 Ready to learn fast. Experience with or willingness to quickly pick up no-code/low-code AI platforms, prompt engineering, and agent configuration. You'll be trained on GitLab's specific tooling, but you should arrive ready to get your hands dirty.
 Strong conceptual understanding of AI capabilities - summarization, classification, generation, automation, agentic workflows - and a commitment to staying current. The landscape shifts constantly. The tools you use today may be obsolete in weeks. You stay on top of new developments so that your org's AI strategy reflects what's actually possible, not what was possible six months ago.
 Ability to map data flows - structured and unstructured. Understand where agents need context, and figure out where humans should interface with automated workflows and at what steps.
 About the team
 You will partner closely with Enterprise AI within the Enterprise Technology & AI organization, while remaining embedded in your own function. Enterprise AI provides the technical delivery capability, platforms, and patterns. You provide the business context, prioritization, building at the no-code layer, and adoption muscle. Together, you form the core of your function's AI transformation.

 ServiceCentral is hiring Partnership & Growth Associates to win new customers and grow the ones we bring in. This is a real sales role from day one: you will build your own pipeline, run your own discovery conversations, deliver your own demos, and carry a quota. New business is the priority here, and prospecting is not something you fit around the edges of your week, it is the heart of the job.
 You will also own accounts outright, which means you get to see the full arc of a customer relationship rather than one slice of it: winning them, getting them live, growing them, and keeping them. You will build real product depth, get hands-on coaching from people who have done this work themselves, and have experienced support in the room when a deal gets complex. What we are looking for in return is drive, curiosity, and a genuine appetite for hitting a number.
 What You Will Own
 Pipeline generation and conversion
 Generate qualified pipeline through outbound calling, email sequences, and social outreach across assigned campaigns, verticals, and territories
 Sustain consistent, high-volume prospecting activity as the anchor of your week
 Manage and qualify inbound leads with fast, accurate follow-up and correct routing
 Research accounts and stakeholders so outreach is personalised rather than generic
 Run discovery conversations using our qualification framework, and deliver online product demonstrations
 Close new business against a quarterly quota
 Hand off opportunities above your authority to Specialists, Managers, or Directors with full context, and earn sourced-pipeline credit
 Route opportunities on the other platform to your counterpart owner, and earn referral credit
 Account ownership
 Own the full commercial relationship for your assigned portfolio of accounts
 Maintain a defined contact cadence so no owned account drifts without engagement
 Execute standard renewals cleanly and on time
 Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities, closing the simple ones and pulling in a Manager or Director on the rest

 Execute defined save plays on accounts showing risk
 Onboarding and time to value
 Own commercial handoff and welcome communications that set clear expectations
 Coordinate onboarding with Solutions and Support so customers reach value quickly
 Track time-to-first-value on your accounts and intervene when it slips
 Act on or route expansion signals that surface during onboarding
 Revenue integrity
 Audit subscription billing on your accounts to prevent revenue leakage
 Monitor involuntary churn signals (failed and declined charges) and drive resolution within 24 hours
 Reconcile the billing platform against internal records so MRR reporting is accurate
 Verify plan changes (upgrades, downgrades, cancellations) are executed correctly before a customer notices an error
 Surface systemic billing patterns to your Manager rather than fixing the same problem repeatedly
 Enablement and team support
 Provide day-to-day support on larger accounts held by senior colleagues: routine maintenance, data updates, configuration changes, and low-complexity requests
 Absorb repeatable work so senior capacity stays on new business and strategic pursuits
 Create and maintain customer-facing Knowledge Base and self-service content that drives adoption and reduces inbound volume
 Verify release notes for accuracy and customer clarity before publication
 Support go-to-market materials and campaign content for upsell and cross-sell motions
 Support trade shows and events: booth materials, collateral, demo environment readiness, on-site coordination, and lead capture with follow-up
 Systems discipline
 Keep CRM records complete and current, with a scheduled next action on every open opportunity
 Log activity accurately, because your forecast and your credit both depend on it

 Commercial drive.  You want to carry a number and you want to beat it.
 Resilience.  High-volume outreach means high-volume rejection. You need to make the next call sound like the first one.

 Process discipline.  You will run recurring operational workflows (billing audits, cadence management, CRM hygiene) that protect revenue. Reliability here is the foundation of customer trust.
 Commercial instinct.  You notice when a routine support question is actually an expansion signal, and you do something about it.

This role is for one of our clients 
 Compensation: $33.58 per hour 
 Fluent Language Skills Required:  Korean. Native fluency in Korean, including full command of Hangul, is required for this position. All annotation and transcription work is performed in Korean.
 Why This Role Exists 
 Document understanding breaks down fastest in the languages that parsing and vision-language models rarely see. This project builds training data for exactly those languages: Korean, alongside Japanese and five Indic scripts. Each task takes a real, publicly available PDF page and produces a complete structural map of that page, paired with a faithful transcription of every text region in the original script.
 The dataset deliberately concentrates on the material models handle worst: handwriting, dense multi-column layouts, tables, diagrams, and mixed-script pages. Documents are drawn from newspapers, textbooks, examinations, and everyday formats such as flyers, forms, manuals, menus, brochures, notices and worksheets, so that the corpus reflects the real diversity of Korean documents rather than a narrow band of easily parsed ones.
 Delivered work is human-authored throughout. Component identification, component typing, reading order and all transcription are performed by people, not generated by parsing models.
 What You'll Do 
 Open and check a task: pages are provided, so you do not source documents yourself. We find the PDFs and upload them for you. Before annotating, confirm the page is in Korean, is legible, has real content, and shows no personal details
 Annotate structure: identify and bound every meaningful region of the page - document title, section heading, paragraph, list, table, figure, diagram, caption, formula, question, answer field - and assign each a component type and a reading-order index
 Record relationships: link each region to the figure or table it belongs to through a parent component identifier
 Transcribe faithfully: reproduce all text exactly as it appears in Hangul, including any hanja and handwritten content, flagging any region where the source is not legible
 Capture page metadata: language, document type, source, page dimensions, and flags for tables, formulas and handwriting
 Review a colleague's work: every task is reviewed end to end by a second Korean expert, and experienced annotators take on that review
 Who You Are 
 You are a native Korean speaker with full command of Hangul, including hanja where it appears in older or formal documents
 You have worked in bilingual transcription, translation, editorial work, or AI training data, ideally with reviewer experience
 You are exact: character-level accuracy matters more here than speed, and a single wrong jamo is a defect
 You are systematic: you apply a taxonomy consistently across hundreds of pages rather than improvising per document
 You are comfortable with unfamiliar layouts: multi-column newspapers, exam papers, handwritten forms
